notes: minutes=null means no timed sitting/no official per-part timing. IA 'minutes' are recommended teaching hours x60, not exam time. Science Paper 1A/1B have no separate official time; see paper1Combined.

subjects.name: Biology

components.name: Paper 1A
components.format: Multiple choice: SL 30 items (SL material only); HL 40 items (SL + additional HL material); 1 mark each, no negative marking
components.notes: Sat together with Paper 1B in one uninterrupted sitting; separate booklet. Paper 1 total: SL 90 min / HL 120 min; IB does not split time between 1A and 1B.

components.name: Paper 1B
components.format: Four data-based questions related to experimental work and the syllabus (syllabus related, addressing all themes)
components.notes: Paper 1 (1A+1B) combined: SL 90 min, 55 marks, 36%; HL 120 min, 75 marks, 36%. Tests AO1-AO3.

components.name: Paper 2
components.format: Section A: data-based question + short-answer questions (SL 34 marks; HL 48 marks). Section B: extended-response questions (SL 16 marks, answer 1 of 2; HL 32 marks, answer 2 of 3)

components.name: Internal assessment: scientific investigation
components.format: Open-ended scientific investigation written up as a report (max 3,000 words); requirements identical at SL and HL
components.notes: Minutes = 10 recommended teaching hours, not a timed sitting. Internally assessed, externally moderated.

assessmentObjectives: AO1 Demonstrate knowledge of terminology, facts and concepts; skills, techniques and methodologies
AO2 Understand and apply knowledge of terminology and concepts; skills, techniques and methodologies
AO3 Analyse, evaluate and synthesize experimental procedures, primary and secondary data, trends, patterns and predictions
AO4 Demonstrate the application of skills necessary to carry out insightful and ethical investigations
subjects.gaps: Guide gives no separate time split between Paper 1A and 1B (secondary sites quoting 45/45 min are unofficial). Collaborative sciences project: compulsory interdisciplinary project (10 recommended teaching hours, SL and HL) shared by all DP sciences; NOT assessed / carries no marks.

subjects.name: Environmental systems and societies (interdisciplinary: Group 3 and/or Group 4)
subjects.curriculumVersion: ESS guide, first assessment 2026 (published Feb 2024; updated through Nov 2025)

components.name: Paper 1
components.format: Unseen case study (resource booklet) with data in various forms; all questions compulsory; analysis and evaluation of the data
components.resources: Case study resource booklet provided in exam
components.notes: Calculator required for both papers; GDCs permitted. Tests AO1-AO3.

components.name: Paper 2
components.format: Section A (40 marks): short-answer and data-based questions. Section B: structured essays, 20 marks each - SL answer 1 of 2 (20 marks); HL answer 2 of 3 (40 marks). Final 9 marks of each essay marked with markbands

components.name: Internal assessment: individual investigation
components.format: Individual investigation of an environmental issue/research question (same criteria SL and HL)

assessmentObjectives: AO1 Knowledge and understanding (concepts, theories, perspectives; data; methods and models; case studies)
AO2 Application and analysis
AO3 Evaluation and synthesis
AO4 Use and application of appropriate skills (identify issue/RQ; select and use methodologies ethically)
subjects.gaps: ESS counts toward Group 3, Group 4 or both. HL is new (first assessed 2026); HL uses three HL lenses (environmental law, environmental/ecological economics, environmental ethics). Guide does not say whether ESS students take part in the collaborative sciences project; not verified.

subjects.name: Computer science
subjects.curriculumVersion: Computer science guide, first assessment 2027 (first teaching Aug 2025)

components.name: Paper 1
components.format: Section A: extended-response questions on Theme A Concepts of computer science (SL 38 marks; HL 56 marks). Section B: questions on the pre-seen case study (SL 12 marks, short-response, 2 challenge questions; HL 24 marks, short- and extended-response, 4 challenges). All compulsory; A and B done together
components.resources: Pre-seen case study released on PRC 12 months before May session (18 months before Nov)
components.notes: Calculator policy not stated in the 2027 guide (outgoing 2014 guide: no calculators in any CS exam).

components.name: Paper 2
components.format: Extended-response questions on Theme B Computational thinking and problem-solving; all compulsory; one question on algorithmic thinking without code; two versions: Python or Java; some built-in functions may be prohibited per question. HL repeats two SL questions plus HL-only questions

components.name: Internal assessment: the computational solution
components.format: Computational solution to a real-world problem of the student's choice

assessmentObjectives: AO1 Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of facts, concepts, principles, terminology and computational-thinking methods
AO2 Apply and use facts, concepts, methods and presentation methods
AO3 Construct, synthesize, analyse and evaluate problem specifications, requirements, success criteria, testing strategies, programs, techniques and solutions
AO4 Demonstrate the application of computational thinking skills to solve real-world problems
subjects.gaps: No Paper 3 and no options in the 2027 course. ibo.org updates page text says '80% external / 20% IA for both levels' but its own table and the guide give SL 70/30, HL 80/20 - use the guide. Calculator policy unverified. Also part of collaborative sciences project (10 h). Outgoing 2014-guide course (see computer-science-legacy) last assessed Nov 2026 (inferred).

components.notes: Calculators not permitted in any CS exam.

components.name: Paper 2 (option)
components.format: Questions on one option (databases, modelling & simulation, web science, OOP-Java). HL: Section A common (45) + Section B HL extension (20)

components.name: Paper 3 (case study)
components.format: Four compulsory structured questions on the annual pre-released case study
components.resources: Clean copy of case study issued with paper

components.name: Internal assessment: solution
components.format: Computational solution (criteria A6 B6 C12 D4 E6)

assessmentObjectives: AO1 Know and understand
AO2 Apply and use
AO3 Construct, analyse, evaluate (and formulate)
AO4 Demonstrate personal and interpersonal skills/use of appropriate techniques (IA)
subjects.gaps: Last assessment year (Nov 2026) inferred from new course first assessment May 2027, not seen in an IB statement. AO4 wording paraphrased (not re-checked).

components.name: Art-making inquiries portfolio

Refine intentions and art-making through investigation, dialogue and critical reflection
Resolve artworks to fulfil intentions and convey meaning
Situate own and others' artworks in context(s), audience(s), communities of practice
Synthesize concept and form through creative and curatorial practices
